findings_addressed.oracle: After undo(), is_modified() must return False because no write operations remain in the undo stack. The oracle is the inverse of the already-tested write path: write sets modified=True, undo must reset it to False, redo must restore it to True. The three-state sequence (False->True->False->True) provides a complete cycle check.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In UndoManager.undo() (or HexDocument.undo()), remove or skip the call that resets the modification flag (e.g., change `self.is_modified = False` to a no-op or delete the reset line) — after this mutation, is_modified() would remain True after undo(), making `assert not sample_doc_from_bytes.is_modified()` fail.

notes: Added `assert not sample_doc_from_bytes.is_modified()` immediately after the undo() call at line 159. This closes the no-assertion gap: the test now verifies the full three-state transition (modified=True after write, modified=False after undo, modified=True after redo). Without this assertion, a broken undo() that failed to reset modification state would pass silently.
